summary: Ghent University's Special Research Fund (BOF) offers 'sandwich' doctoral scholarships to candidates from Global South countries: you spend part of your PhD in Ghent, funded by the university, and part at a partner institution at home.
covers: A PhD scholarship for 24 months of research at Ghent University.
A bench fee of €310 per month of research in Ghent and an €8,000 travel budget, paid to the Ghent supervisor for the project.
The other half of the research happens in the Global South and must be funded full-time by the partner institution there.
eligibility: Nationality of a country on Ghent University's Global South country list.
The explicit commitment of a Ghent University professor to act as your PhD supervisor.
Mandatory co-funding: a partner institution in the South that provides full-time PhD support for 24 months.
At least 36 months of doctoral work remaining when the scholarship starts.
how_to_apply: Find a Ghent supervisor whose research matches yours and agree a joint project with a home institution.
Secure written co-funding for the 24 months in the South.
Your supervisor and you submit the application to the BOF office — the 2026 call closed on 17 February 2026.
Results are announced from late May, for a start on 1 October.
watch_out: This is only half of a PhD's funding. Without the home institution's 24 months of funding, you cannot apply.
Supervisors receive many requests; a focused, well-researched email is essential.
Check the current Global South country list — it is updated.

sources.title: Ghent University — Doctoral scholarships for candidates from the Global South (BOF)
